title: Building my first iOS game with Claude Code. Ship 4 levels or build more?
author: Few-Distribution9652
selftext:
After a 6-year break, my first project back was ([BlinkAway: Break Reminders](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/blinkaway-break-reminders/id6760686476?mt=12)) , a small Mac app built with Claude. Now I'm making my first game: a 2D iOS platformer in Unity, using Claude Code.

I have 4 levels done, no public build yet. Built it in Unity and Blender, mostly with Claude Opus 5.5, though I used Sonnet for smaller fixes and refactors.  
  
Should I polish and launch this small version first, then add levels from feedback? Or keep building until it feels complete?

comments.author: hyperg8_games
comments.body: from my experience I would ship small. My "dream project" flopped on CrazyGames, so I pivoted to smaller games, and those taught me way more about platform-fit and what players actually want than building the big thing did. To be honest my experience is only with web platforms, not the iOS App Store, so I cant really tell how the store side works there (ranking, reviews, first impression on the store page). But before building level 5 I would put the 4 levels in front of real players, TestFlight or even a quick Unity WebGL build, and see where they die, where they quit and if they even reach level 4. With Claude Code more levels are the cheap part anyway, the hard part is knowing which levels are actually fun, and only players can tell you that. What mechanic is carrying the levels right now?

replies.author: Few-Distribution9652
replies.body:
You just kill waves of enemies to progress. At levels 2 & 4 you encounter boss fights.   
I am just vibe coding this thing, but I like your idea. I need to integrate analytics to know how players are progressing.   
About the App Store I am also pretty much clueless. Maybe something to figure out.
